x: What a semi-final it was too with Michael Johnson, Frankie Fredericks and Robson Da Silva in the field. Adeniken of Nigeria ran a very strong race and our man was shut out of the final by five hundredths.
At the Monte Carlo Grand Prix on August 3rd, in his speciality distance the 200 metres, John Regis came up against his main rivals Michael Johnson and Frankie Fredericks.
He was only a few metres down on Black, World Champion Pettigrew and British Record holder Derek Redmond, although Michael Johnson was in a class of his own with 43.98.

A 20.62 win in round 1 of the longer race showed that he meant business and then later in the day another victory came in the quarter-finals where 20.43 gave him a startling margin over the favourite, Michael Johnson of the USA.

John is now rated at no. 21 of all time taking into consideration the 100/200/400. All the big names feature in the list, headed by Michael Johnson and ranging from Tommie Smith in '68 through to Quincy Watts in '92.

John Regis warmed up with a 10.45 'hundred' (+0.9) and then faced Carl Lewis, Michael Johnson, Mike Marsh, etc. in the 200m (+1.1). His 20.25 for 4th was impressive as he was more or less line abreast with his rivals as they hit the straight.
Du'aine Ladejo faded a little but still clocked a low 46 run after following Michael Johnson's blistering pace, the American preferring the Euro circuit to that of the US.

The race was won by Michael Johnson in 19.94 with Fredericks 3rd - the second time he had been beaten by Regis in a week. What a brilliant night for fast Belgrave times, for Du'aine Ladejo made a third improvement on his best one lap time while equalling Black's fastest British time for the year and…

Stars from overseas who have competed whilst I have been here include Gwen Torrence, Michael Johnson, Mike Powell and Sergei Bubka, as well as Linford Christie and Colin Jackson, who are regular visitors to Sydney to train in the European off season.
A certain American by the name of Michael Johnson would have to be everyone's favourite but let's face it, any American who makes the Games is going to be red hot.
